assertions.assert: With a database it opens it (migrating it to the head revision through the memory ability) and is ready: it sends `bot.ability.offers` `{ability: "stm", choices: []}` once; without one it is ready the same way, holds nothing (records and turns are dropped) and answers every read empty.

`bot.ability.memory.stm.record` `{stimulus_name, payload, event_id?, source?, target?}` is written with no reply, and `bot.ability.memory.stm.recent` `{stimulus_name?, limit?}` answers `bot.ability.memory.stm.recent.output` `{entries}`: the records inside the recency window, newest first, each `{stm_id, stimulus_name, payload, event_id, source, target, created_at, last_accessed_at}`, optionally only one stimulus's, at most `limit`.

Each record evicts, in its own transaction, every record beyond `capacity` by the effective clock (last access, else admission), so the register holds the newest `capacity`; a read past `recency_window_ms` finds nothing.
`bot.ability.memory.stm.reinforce` `{stm_ids}` stamps those records' `last_accessed_at` (no reply), which moves their effective clock forward for reads and eviction.

`bot.ability.memory.stm.turn` `{id, direction, speakers, text, cut, conversation}` is written with no reply, and `bot.ability.memory.stm.recent_turns` `{limit?, within?}` answers `bot.ability.memory.stm.recent_turns.output` `{turns}`: the newest turns, at most `limit`, oldest first, each `{id, at, direction, speakers, text, cut, conversation}` with `at` UTC (Z).
A turn that puts the register over `turn_capacity` sheds the older half at once, in the same transaction: the newest `turn_capacity - floor(turn_capacity / 2)` stay.
A turn's words longer than 2048 UTF-8 bytes are cut at a whole word and its `cut` is true; words that cut to nothing (only white space before the bound) are not written.

The turns' window is `turn_window_ms`, or `within` (milliseconds) when that is shorter; its floor moves in whole steps of half the window, so a turn is read for at least the window and at most one and a half windows.
Requests and notifications are applied one at a time, in arrival order: what arrives while it is opening or applying waits, so a read sees every write sent before it.

A database it cannot open leaves it degraded, without an offer: it sends `bot.ability.failed` `{message: "unavailable: StmMemory is degraded."}`, answers every request the same way, and drops every notification.
